chapter_title: Concerning Food: It shall be allocated to Five Products of the human Body.
chapter_note: After a brief hagiographic opening formula, the chapter is a compact five-fold, impersonal teaching on how sustenance is distributed into five bodily ‘productions’. There are no Gospel citations, no institutional application, and no exhortation; the discourse stays within a systematic degree-structure (food → five products), consistent with the oldest teaching style despite the non-cosmological subject matter.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue-frame opener (‘Once again… to his disciples’), characteristic of the later Kephalaia editorial apparatus.

paragraphs.core_text: This sustenance of various kinds that people gather in and eat, and enters the body; it shall be distributed to five productions.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, structural exposition introducing a numbered five-fold scheme (distribution into five), without address, polemic, or institutional anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: The first product is this that shall issue from the person in rapture and rises up in the Mind, and it comes out from all his limbs, and is immeasurable.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered item in a systematic series; descriptive ‘what it is/does’ voice with internal body-terms (‘Mind’, ‘limbs’), not applied to church or moral instruction.

paragraphs.core_text: The second is this that shall issue from the person in voice and word.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the numbered five-fold list in the same impersonal expository register.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is this that shall spring from them in strength and activity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Same five-fold structural style; no editorial seam or application-voice markers.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth is what is engendered by the pleasure of lu[s]t in men and women.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still itemized description within the five-fold production scheme; no exhortation or institutional mapping despite sexual vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth is this that shall be formed and sculpted in the flesh, and be engendered and come from them. It is this corporeal creature; only its parents can recognise this creature that they beget. They are attentive to its desire and its thought and its [lo]ve every day, all the time. However, these other four forms they neither notice nor are concerned about; because they are not displayed.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the fifth item with explanatory contrast (visible fifth vs. unnoticed four). The rhetoric remains descriptive rather than hortatory, and does not pivot to contemporary institutions—suggesting core teaching rather than pastoral application.
